houses.title: October Alpha Picks: Earnings Delivery Amid Macro Uncertainty
points: September was a macro-led sell-off (JCI −7.9% MoM). Tech, infrastructure and property fell the most.
An October rebound depends on bond yields stabilising, less pressure on the rupiah and slower foreign selling.
Rotating from macro beta to company-specific earnings catalysts ahead of 3Q26 results and the 27–28 Oct Fed meeting.
To watch: short selling is being phased back in, starting with ASII, BBCA, BRPT, BUMI and INDF, and the minimum share price is now Rp1.

houses.title: IF26 wrap: Some improvement in investor sentiment
points: Foreign investors at IF26 were less bearish than three months ago: lower risk premium, attractive valuation, less policy noise.
MSCI remains an overhang until Nov 2026. Most investors see low risk of a downgrade to Frontier, but expect no additions for a while.
QTD foreign flows: +US$1.3bn into bonds versus −US$221m out of equities. The 10Y government bond yield is stable at ~7.1%.
CLSA expects 1–2 BI rate hikes before year-end. If foreign inflows return, they should favour big caps. BCA remains the top pick.

houses.title: Alpha – 4Q26F outlook: Entering choppy waters
points: Domestic fund cash levels have fallen to 6.2% (4-yr avg 7.3%), so the next leg of any rally needs foreign buying.
Brent above US$100/bbl and expected Fed hikes are the main headwinds, given the 3% fiscal deficit cap.
Base case for the Oct-26 MSCI review: the freeze is extended with a neutral comment. Labour and anti-corruption bills are 4Q risks.
Top picks tilted away from cyclicals: ISAT added, BBNI and BFIN removed. Commodities remain the main source of earnings growth.

houses.title: Back onto the well-trodden path
points: Indonesia's macro anchors (the 3% deficit cap and orthodox BI hikes in defence of the rupiah) have held through every stress episode since 2001.
Market bottoms have historically formed only after rupiah pressure eases, so currency stabilisation comes first.
The JCI trades at 8.1x 1Y forward P/E, 2.6 standard deviations below its 5Y mean. Earnings carry downside risk, but cash flows and balance sheets are solid.
Tail risks: MSCI classification and the FTSE rebalance. S&P's sovereign affirmation helps sentiment.
